key_insight: Training a generative diffusion "meta-model" on a large corpus of LLM residual-stream activations lets you learn the true distribution of internal states, enabling structure discovery and higher‑fidelity interventions without strong structural assumptions.
problem_solved: Existing activation-analysis tools (e.g., PCA, sparse autoencoders) impose rigid assumptions and provide weak priors for interventions; this paper addresses the need for a flexible, generative prior that models activations directly and improves analysis and intervention fidelity.
method: Collect large-scale residual-stream activations from an LLM (≈1 billion activations) and train diffusion-based generative models to learn the distribution of those internal states.
Use the trained diffusion meta-model for tasks such as reconstruction, sampling, and counterfactual interventions in activation space, treating the model as a learned prior over activations.
Compare behavior and intervention fidelity against standard baselines (e.g., PCA, sparse autoencoders) to evaluate the meta-model's utility for interpretability and control.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a practical, assumption-light tool for probing, sampling, and intervening in LLM internal representations—improving interpretability, more reliable causal interventions, and tooling for debugging and safety research.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: LLM -> residual activations (1B) -> diffusion meta-model training -> sampling/reconstruction/intervention
Bar/line chart: reconstruction/intervention fidelity comparison (diffusion meta-model vs PCA vs sparse autoencoder)
Latent/activation manifold visualization: t-SNE/UMAP of true activations with samples from the meta-model overlaid
Before/after intervention example: input, original activation trajectory and output vs modified activation trajectory and resulting output
paper_title: Learning a Generative Meta-Model of LLM Activations
paper_authors: Grace Luo, Jiahai Feng, Trevor Darrell, Alec Radford, Jacob Steinhardt
